answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust is a bounded-length random walk whose transition mass is diluted when it encounters sparse boundaries. A sybil cluster therefore appears as a low-conductance set: its small external cut limits escape probability, so min-cut transitivity bounds cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight regardless of its internal size. Honest attestations remain the tide, each verified edge a relic of provenance, while the trusted core acts as an oasis.
